paper_title: Exact solution of the frustrated Potts model with next-nearest-neighbor interactions in one dimension via AI bootstrapping (Yin, 2025, Physical Review Letters)
deeper_reasoning_2:
\section*{Claim}
The field-Potts model is thermodynamically equivalent to the frustrated $J_1$-$J_2$ chain because both positive transfer problems have the same Perron quotient matrix.  For
\[
K(a,b)=x^{\delta(a,b)}y^{\delta(a,1)+\delta(b,1)},
\qquad x=e^{\beta J_2},\quad y=e^{\beta J_1/2},
\]
and
\[
|\phi_1\rangle=|1\rangle,
\qquad
|\phi_2\rangle=(q-1)^{-1/2}\sum_{s=2}^{q}|s\rangle,
\]
the restriction of $K$ to $\mathcal N=\operatorname{span}\{|\phi_1\rangle,|\phi_2\rangle\}$ is
\[
K|_{\mathcal N}=\begin{pmatrix}xy^2&\sqrt{q-1}\,y\\\sqrt{q-1}\,y&x+q-2\end{pmatrix}=T_2.
\]
Consequently both models have the same largest one-step transfer eigenvalue and the same thermodynamic free energy per spin.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &K(a,b)=x^{\delta(a,b)}y^{\delta(a,1)+\delta(b,1)}\text{ for }a,b\in\{1,\ldots,q\}.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &K\text{ is positive and is invariant under permutations of labels }2,\ldots,q.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\text{A positive invariant transfer matrix has its Perron eigenvector in the fixed subspace}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{The frustrated chain has Perron quotient }T_2
=\begin{pmatrix}xy^2&\sqrt{q-1}\,y\\\sqrt{q-1}\,y&x+q-2\end{pmatrix}.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{For a positive transfer matrix, the thermodynamic free energy is }-\beta^{-1}\ln\lambda,
\text{ where }\lambda\text{ is its Perron eigenvalue per spin}.
\end{aligned}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
The fixed subspace of the permutations of labels $2,\ldots,q$ is exactly
\begin{align}
\mathcal N&=\operatorname{span}\{|\phi_1\rangle,|\phi_2\rangle\},
\end{align}
because a fixed vector has one coefficient at state $1$ and one common coefficient on all states $2,\ldots,q$.  By (P2) and (P3), the Perron eigenvector of $K$ lies in $\mathcal N$.

The matrix elements of $K$ in the orthonormal basis $(|\phi_1\rangle,|\phi_2\rangle)$ are
\begin{align}
\langle\phi_1|K|\phi_1\rangle
&=K(1,1)=xy^2,\\
\langle\phi_1|K|\phi_2\rangle
&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{q-1}}\sum_{s=2}^{q}K(1,s)
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{q-1}}\sum_{s=2}^{q}y
=\sqrt{q-1}\,y,\\
\langle\phi_2|K|\phi_1\rangle
&=\sqrt{q-1}\,y,\\
\langle\phi_2|K|\phi_2\rangle
&=\frac{1}{q-1}\sum_{r=2}^{q}\sum_{s=2}^{q}K(r,s)\\
&=\frac{1}{q-1}\left((q-1)x+(q-1)(q-2)\right)=x+q-2.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
K|_{\mathcal N}&=\begin{pmatrix}xy^2&\sqrt{q-1}\,y\\\sqrt{q-1}\,y&x+q-2\end{pmatrix}=T_2.
\end{align}
Since the Perron eigenvalue of $K$ is the Perron eigenvalue of this quotient and the frustrated chain has the same quotient by (P4),
\begin{align}
\lambda_{\mathrm{field}}&=\lambda_{J_1-J_2},\\
f_{\mathrm{field}}&=-\beta^{-1}\ln\lambda_{\mathrm{field}}
=-\beta^{-1}\ln\lambda_{J_1-J_2}=f_{J_1-J_2}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{K|_{\mathcal N}=T_2,
\qquad \lambda_{\mathrm{field}}=\lambda_{J_1-J_2},
\qquad f_{\mathrm{field}}=f_{J_1-J_2}.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

deeper_metadata.revision_intent: Improve alignment by making the zero-temperature phase labels explicit, separating exact residual-entropy claims from controlled low-temperature approximations, and ensuring every derivation advances beyond a direct restatement of core reasoning.

rubric_interpretation.top_level_schema: Only paper_title, contiguous deeper_reasoning_k strings, and one deeper_metadata object are used.
rubric_interpretation.latex_constraint: Each deeper_reasoning_k is a standalone LaTeX fragment requiring only article, amsmath, and amssymb.
rubric_interpretation.high_value_standard: A derivation is selected only if it fuses multiple core facts, supplies a missing mechanistic bridge, or makes a goal-critical implicit step explicit.

deeper_reasoning_1.title: Perron-symmetric quotient theorem for the exact thermodynamic solution
major_advancement_modes: unifies invariant-block construction with Perron dominance
connects the squared ladder spectrum to the one-step thermodynamic factor
deeper_reasoning_1.goal_alignment: Directly proves the arbitrary-q closed form for lambda and f.
deeper_reasoning_1.scientific_payoff: Explains why a q^2-dimensional transfer problem collapses to a two-dimensional Perron quotient.
deeper_reasoning_1.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Turns two separate core derivations into one dominance theorem.
deeper_reasoning_1.formal_sharpness: Covers all q>=2, beta>0, and real J1,J2 under the positivity of the ladder matrix.
deeper_reasoning_1.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids redoing all entrywise orbit sums from core_reasoning_1.
controlled_external_lemmas: Perron-Frobenius uniqueness for positive finite matrices
deeper_reasoning_1.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Relies on the supplied identity T_lad=T_ov^2; this is explicit in the source goals/core.

deeper_reasoning_2.goal_alignment: Directly proves equality of dominant block, lambda, and free energy for the source and field models.
deeper_reasoning_2.scientific_payoff: Clarifies that the mapping is thermodynamic equivalence in the Perron sector, not a superficial analogy.
deeper_reasoning_2.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Elevates the block calculation into a reusable relevant-subspace matching argument while staying within the paper's established family.
deeper_reasoning_2.formal_sharpness: Applies for every q>=2, beta>0, and real J1,J2.
deeper_reasoning_2.low_value_rejection_audit: Does not introduce unsupported mappings to unrelated Hamiltonians.
controlled_external_lemmas: Perron vector lies in the fixed subspace of a positive symmetry-invariant transfer matrix
deeper_reasoning_2.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The broader subspace-matching programme is mentioned only as a criterion instantiated by this exact family.

An exact finite-temperature phase-boundary claim based only on low-temperature sector free energies.

global_alignment_audit.schema: Compliant: one JSON object; allowed top-level keys only; contiguous deeper_reasoning_1 through deeper_reasoning_5; one deeper_metadata object.
global_alignment_audit.proof_value: High: each derivation either integrates multiple core proofs, supplies a missing bridge, or explains a mechanism required by the goals.
global_alignment_audit.goal_coverage: Full coverage of G1, G2, and G3, including explicit phase labels and entropy gaps.
global_alignment_audit.core_coverage: Covers all six supplied core_reasoning entries without relying on unsupported external claims.
global_alignment_audit.overclaim_control: The only finite-temperature formulas are explicitly scoped as low-temperature large-q sector estimates, not exact phase boundaries.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The derivations rely on premises extracted in core_01.json and goals_01.json rather than re-proving the Hamiltonian-to-transfer-matrix construction from first principles.

The controlled large-q sector comparison is kept subordinate to the exact entropy-gap proof.
